TITLE: Goodwill Accounting
ALIASES:
DESCRIPTION: This document covers the recognition, calculation, and treatment of goodwill as an intangible asset.
SUMMARY: The document addresses how goodwill is recognized when a firm is purchased, detailing the calculation method and its classification as an intangible asset. The conclusion is that goodwill is subject to impairment testing under certain accounting standards.
ORG: FASB || WHY: They removed the option to use the pooling-of-interests method for recording business combinations.
ORG: Private Company Council of the FASB || WHY: They established an accounting alternative for amortizing goodwill for private companies.
ORG: Accounting Standards Board || WHY: They are involved in setting rules that are subject to change regarding goodwill accounting treatment.
CONCEPT: Intangible Asset || WHY: Goodwill is classified as an intangible asset on the balance sheet.
CONCEPT: Acquisition Premium || WHY: Goodwill reflects the premium the buyer pays over the net value of other assets.
CONCEPT: Impairment Testing || WHY: Management is responsible for determining if an impairment is required for goodwill.
FACT: Goodwill is recognized when a firm is purchased as a going concern. || SECTION: Goodwill (accounting)
FACT: To calculate goodwill, the fair market value of acquired assets and liabilities is deducted from the purchase price. || SECTION: Calculating goodwill
FACT: If company A acquired company B and paid $20, goodwill would be $11 ($20 - $9). || SECTION: Calculating goodwill
FACT: Goodwill is considered to have an indefinite useful life under U.S. GAAP and IFRS for public companies. || SECTION: Goodwill (accounting)
FACT: Goodwill can only be impaired under current GAAP standards. || SECTION: Amortization and adjustments to carrying value
